title: Telnet service exposed on local and upstream interfaces
impact: A local network attacker may reach the Telnet-like login service. If weak or hardcoded credentials exist, this may allow remote administrative or shell access.
recommendation: Disable Telnet by default and replace it with SSH only if remote administration is required.

title: Web interface allows login without user-supplied credentials
impact: Any user connected to the repeater management network can click Login and access the admin interface.
recommendation: Require users to create a unique admin password during first setup.

title: Default admin credentials exposed in login page HTML
impact: The login page reveals hidden username and default password values.
recommendation: Remove hardcoded credentials from client-side HTML.

title: Admin credentials stored in Base64 Authorization cookie
impact: The cookie can expose admin credentials because Base64 is not encryption and the cookie is not HttpOnly or Secure.
recommendation: Use secure server-side session tokens with HttpOnly, Secure, and SameSite attributes.

title: DNS resolver exposed upstream with setup-domain redirection
impact: The repeater exposes DNS behavior and resolves zrlogin.cn to its internal management IP.
recommendation: Restrict DNS exposure to required interfaces only.

title: No logout option to terminate admin session
impact: Users cannot explicitly terminate the admin session from the interface.
recommendation: Add a logout function that clears and invalidates the session.

title: Admin credentials exposed in URL query parameters during login
impact: Credentials may be stored in browser history, logs, screenshots, and network captures.
recommendation: Submit credentials using POST over HTTPS and never place passwords in URLs.
